correctness.rationale: The hub-normalized feasible set is a compact Lipschitz polytope with positive-definite centered variance Hessian, so every maximizer is a vertex. Components of tight rim edges must meet a spoke bound, yielding exactly four possible levels for 1/2<t<1. Exact pairwise-variance algebra excludes one-extreme-sign vertices; counting the number of smaller-level rim vertices, with an odd-parity sign-sum comparison, excludes all configurations with more than two interfaces. Construction meets the bound and fixes all equality cases. At t=1 use the quadratic rescaling sandwich and a separate ternary-level integer argument. The two formulas give the derivative jump by direct differentiation. The included exact-rational checker independently confirms 45 (n,t) settings including 218571 feasible four-level labelled assignments and symbolically guided competitor comparisons; finite checks do not replace the proof.
